results.title: Slow Internet Speeds Troubleshooting
results.snippet: 1. **Weak modem signal** — downstream signal below -7 dBmV or above +7 dBmV indicates line issues. 2. **WiFi interference or distance** — 2.4 GHz band congestion; customer too far from router. 3. **Peak-hour congestion** — shared neighbourhood node oversubscribed in the evenings (6–10 PM).

results.title: Modem Reboot Procedure
results.snippet: Reboot the modem when the customer reports: - No internet connection despite modem appearing powered on - Very slow speeds that did not improve after router restart

results.title: WiFi vs. Ethernet — Troubleshooting Connectivity Differences
results.snippet: | Factor | Ethernet (wired) | WiFi (wireless) | |---|---|---| | Speed | Full subscribed tier | Up to 80% of tier (varies by band) |

results.title: Device Compatibility — Approved Modems and Routers
results.snippet: Customers must use a modem on the ISP-approved list to receive full technical support. Unapproved modems may work but are not guaranteed to provision correctly or receive remote management commands (including `reboot_modem_remotely`).

results.title: DNS Issues Troubleshooting
results.snippet: - Websites fail to load but the customer can ping IP addresses directly (e.g., `ping 8.8.8.8` succeeds). - Browser shows "DNS_PROBE_FINISHED_NXDOMAIN" or "Server Not Found" errors. - Some websites work but others do not, seemingly at random.

tickets.issue: Slow internet speeds in the evening
tickets.resolution: Peak-hour node congestion. Customer advised to switch to 5 GHz WiFi band and schedule large downloads for off-peak hours.

tickets.issue: No internet connection after power outage
tickets.resolution: Modem rebooted remotely. Service restored within 3 minutes.

tickets.issue: Intermittent WiFi drops throughout the day
tickets.resolution: Field technician found corroded coax connector at wall plate. Connector replaced. Signal levels normalised.

data.text:
<analysis>
**Key Findings:**

1. **Account & Equipment** [tool:lookup_customer]: Jane has an active Gigabit 500 service tier with a NETGEAR CM500 modem and TP-Link Archer AX21 router since 2021.

2. **Critical Signal Issue** [tool:check_modem_status]: The modem shows **weak signal quality** with downstream signal at **-12 dBmV** (outside acceptable range; should be between -7 and +7 dBmV per KB). The modem has restarted **7 times in the last 24 hours** and uptime is only 0.5 hours—indicating instability.

3. **Network Performance Degraded** [tool:ping_customer_modem]: High latency (287 ms) and 12.5% packet loss detected, consistent with a signal or line issue.

4. **No ISP-Level Outage** [tool:check_isp_outage]: No active outages in zip code 10001.

5. **Recurring Pattern** [tool:get_ticket_history]: Jane reported the same issue (slow evening speeds) on April 28, which was attributed to peak-hour node congestion and resolved by switching to 5 GHz WiFi. However, this time the root cause appears different—the modem signal is genuinely weak and unstable, not just congestion.

6. **KB Guidance** [kb:slow_speeds]: Weak downstream signal (Jane's -12 dBmV is well outside the -7 to +7 range) indicates a line issue, not WiFi congestion. This is more serious than the previous ticket.

**Diagnosis**: The modem's weak downstream signal and frequent restarts suggest a **physical line problem** (loose connector, signal degradation, or line noise) rather than simple congestion. This needs escalation to a field technician or line inspection.
</analysis>
